transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I just… I feel restless all the time. Like there’s a motor running inside me. If I have to sit still, like at church or here at the clinic, even at home, I start feeling trapped and I need to get up or do something.
Did this restless feeling start after you began taking, stopped taking, or changed the dose of any medication?
I don’t think so. I can’t really tie it to any medicine change or anything like that.
Did you already feel this kind of restlessness when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. In school, when I was a kid, teachers used to move my seat a lot because I couldn’t stay still. I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and sometimes I’d get up before class was even over. Got in trouble for that.
Do you often have trouble focusing on tasks or conversations, even when you want to pay attention?

Yeah… I do. I’ll be listening at first, like if someone’s telling me ride times, or what needs picked up from the pantry, or plans for church, and then… my mind just kind of slips off. Then I miss parts I needed.
Have these problems with sitting still or paying attention caused trouble for you at work, school, or in relationships?

Yeah… it has. People at church, and the pantry, even my family… they don’t really trust me with rides or appointments or supplies like they used to. I mess it up, or forget parts, and… I feel like I keep letting everybody down, even when I’m trying to help.
Do you ever get sudden rushes of intense fear or panic?
I don’t know… not really. I mean, I get worked up sometimes, but sudden panic like that… I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when you don’t want to?
Not really… I mean, I think about stuff, sure, but I don’t know if I’d call it a lot of worrying about everything. I haven’t really noticed it like that.
